key_bets: Beam-driven non-equilibrium plasma can sustain T_i >> T_e at ~150-250 keV ion temperatures, suppressing bremsstrahlung losses well below thermalized Maxwellian levels
FRC confinement scaling holds across an ~80-150× extrapolation in ion temperature from C-2W (~1-3 keV) to Da Vinci (~250 keV) with no validated transport scaling law
Net energy gain (Q_plasma > 1) can be achieved for p-B11 fuel in a magnetically confined plasma, which has never been demonstrated in any device
FRC tilt and rotational MHD instabilities can be stabilized by tangential NBI at reactor-scale dimensions (1-2 m major radius, multi-MA plasma current), a 2.5-5× scale-up from C-2W
NBI wall-plug-to-plasma efficiency at Da Vinci-class beam energies (proton beams at 250+ keV) can reach 0.20-0.35 or better at commercial scale
The Inverse Cyclotron Converter (ICC) can achieve >90% direct conversion efficiency on MeV-range alpha particles, enabling the long-term economic case (Branch C)
Steady-state CW FRC operation can be sustained from the current ~30-40 ms NBI-pulse-limited record to seconds-to-continuous timescales required for commercial power
eliminated_costs: Tritium breeding blanket (no Li-6 enrichment, no FLiBe, no breeding/extraction infrastructure) — entire CAS account category removed
Heavy neutron shielding (only thin water/boron shield needed for minimal secondary neutrons vs. multi-meter composite shields in D-T)
Remote handling robotics for radioactive maintenance (hands-on maintenance possible due to aneutronic fuel; ITER-class remote handling >$500M avoided)
REBCO HTS magnet supply chain (near-unity FRC beta allows resistive copper coils at ~1 kG external field instead of high-field superconducting magnets)
Tritium handling, accounting, and radiological containment infrastructure for the primary circuit
novel_costs: NBI system as dominant capital account (~$260M, >50% of CAS22 at $10M/MW × 26 MW) — replaces magnets+blanket as the largest cost driver
Continuous NBI recirculating power burden (~100 MW wall-plug at baseline) that cannot be amortized over short pulses, driving Q_plasma requirement to ≥25-35
Inverse Cyclotron Converter (ICC) direct conversion hardware (~$127M in Branch C) — bespoke MHz-frequency power conditioning for ~5 MHz ICC output, no commercial precedent
Specialized high-energy NBI components (negative-ion sources at 250+ keV, neutralization cells, beam dumps) with no commercial manufacturing pathway at fusion scale
Continuous electrical power consumption for resistive copper coil operation (vs. cryogenic costs for superconducting magnets)

risks.description: Bremsstrahlung losses exceed fusion power at thermalized p-B11 conditions (f_rad > 0.7 forces Branch A regardless of Q_plasma); T_i >> T_e suppression strategy unvalidated above ~1 keV
Q_plasma > 1 has never been demonstrated for p-B11 in any confinement device; Branch A (no LCOE, concept non-viable) is a real outcome below Q ≈ 14
~80-150× ion temperature extrapolation from C-2W (~1-3 keV) to Da Vinci (~250 keV) with no validated FRC confinement scaling law
FRC tilt/rotational instabilities at 2.5-5× scale-up to reactor dimensions (1-2 m major radius, multi-MA current) may require additional NBI power for stabilization beyond heating needs
NBI wall-plug-to-plasma efficiency revised down to 0.20-0.35 (from prior 0.55 single-step estimate) per C-2W data, doubling Q_plasma commercial threshold to 25-35
ICC direct conversion at TRL 2-3 with zero experimental demonstration on MeV-range fusion alphas; without ICC, Da Vinci steam-only LCOE (~$119/MWh) is uncompetitive vs. D-T concepts

Capacity factor and recirculating power interact multiplicatively — sub-unity CF (60-75% plausible for FOAK) raises effective recirculating fraction since NBI must stay near full power for FRC stability
Current C-2W FRC pulse record is ~30-40 ms (NBI-pulse-limited); steady-state CW operation at reactor-relevant temperatures and densities undemonstrated
No commercial supply chain or manufacturing pathway exists for reactor-scale high-energy NBI systems (negative-ion sources, neutralization cells, multi-MW power supplies)
Da Vinci commercial design parameters (fusion power, Q value, NBI specs, plasma geometry, capital cost) are entirely unpublished — six blocking data gaps prevent closed LCOE modeling
High-energy proton NBI neutralization is less mature than deuterium NBI (positive-ion gas cell efficiency falls above ~120 keV; negative-ion approaches more complex)
First-wall heat flux management for alpha particle energy deposition in linear FRC geometry is undisclosed; differs structurally from toroidal blanket designs
